## Problem 1
```{r}
set.seed(8105)

has_shared_birthday = function(group_size) {
  birthdays = sample.int(365, size = group_size, replace = TRUE)
  anyDuplicated(birthdays) > 0L
}

birthday_results =
  tibble(group_size = 2:50) |>
  mutate(
    probability = map_dbl(
      group_size,
      \(size) mean(replicate(10000, has_shared_birthday(size)))
    )
  )

birthday_results |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray65") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, color = "#256D85") +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, color = "#256D85") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of a shared birthday",
    x = "Number of people",
    y = "Estimated probability"
  )
```
The estimated probability of at least two people sharing a birthday increases with group size and reaches approximately 50% at 23 people.

## Problem 2
```{r}
subject_files =
  tibble(
    file_path = list.files(path = "data", full.names = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    file_name = basename(file_path),
    observations = purrr::map(
      file_path,
      \(path) read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
    )
  )

longitudinal_df =
  subject_files |>
  select(file_name, observations) |>
  mutate(file_name = str_remove(file_name, "\\.csv$")) |>
  separate_wider_delim(
    file_name,
    delim = "_",
    names = c("arm", "subject_id")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    arm = factor(
      arm,
      levels = c("con", "exp"),
      labels = c("Control", "Experimental")
    )
  ) |>
  unnest(observations) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("week_"),
    names_to = "week",
    names_prefix = "week_",
    names_transform = list(week = as.integer),
    values_to = "observation"
  )

longitudinal_df
```

```{r}
longitudinal_df |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = week,
      y = observation,
      group = interaction(arm, subject_id),
      color = arm
    )
  ) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(vars(arm)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8) +
  labs(
    title = "Weekly observations by study arm",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Observation"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
Observations generally increased over time in the experimental arm, while those in the control arm fluctuated without a clear upward trend. All 10 participants in the experimental arm had higher observations at week 8 than at week 1.
